title: Socratic checklist — quantitative synthesis & certainty (分析)
rationale: Questions the agent must answer before and during synthesis; each answer is recorded for the gate. Sources are chapter/item-level references.

items.question: Is the effect measure and scale chosen to match the outcome type and the certificate's hypothesis?
items.rationale: Mismatched effect measures (e.g., OR for common outcomes) distort interpretation.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.6 (choosing effect measures)

items.question: Is the synthesis model (fixed/random/multilevel) pre-specified and consistent with the study design structure?
items.rationale: Model choice changes point estimates and CI widths; post-hoc switching is p-hacking.
items.answer_format: pre-registered model + design structure it reflects

items.question: Is heterogeneity reported (I2, tau2, prediction interval) and interpreted clinically, not just numerically?
items.rationale: A numeric I2 without clinical interpretation misleads readers.

items.question: Is the pooling decision based on clinical, methodological, and statistical poolability — never on 'tools available'?
items.rationale: Pooling incomparable studies produces meaningless estimates.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.12 (Synthesis Without Meta-analysis, SWiM); Ch.10

items.question: Are small-study effects and reporting bias assessed (funnel, Egger-type, PET-PEESE) and interpreted with the known caveats?
items.rationale: Small-study effects are a leading cause of exaggerated pooled effects.

items.question: Are sensitivity and influence analyses (leave-one-out, model switching, high-RoB exclusion) pre-specified and executed?
items.rationale: Unplanned sensitivity analysis is indistinguishable from specification search.

items.question: Are subgroup and meta-regression analyses limited to the certificate's pre-specified moderators (to control multiplicity)?
items.rationale: Exploratory subgroup fishing inflates false positives.
items.answer_format: prespecified moderator list + any post-hoc analyses flagged

items.question: For network meta-analysis: are transitivity and consistency assumptions checked (node splitting, design-by-treatment)?
items.rationale: NMA without transitivity/consistency checks is unreliable.

items.question: Is certainty (GRADE) assessed per outcome across the five domains, with every downgrade/upgrade recorded with a reason?
items.rationale: Undocumented GRADE decisions make certainty claims unfalsifiable.
items.source: GRADE Handbook (five domains); Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.14

items.question: Do the conclusions match the certainty of evidence (no over-claiming beyond the GRADE level)?
items.rationale: Overstated conclusions are the most common review-level error.
